messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 19
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: Middle Eastern
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Environmental Scientist
  trauma_type: Physical abuse by caregiver (childhood)
  pcl5: 36

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Arguments: Arguments, Affective Expression: Crying, Tactile (Unexpected Touch): Being touched unprepared
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Conflict: Any situation that might involve disagreement or confrontation, Avoid Being Alone: Being alone in a room or building, Avoid People: avoid other people
  Threat: Back to Wall: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room, Safe Seat Seeking: I always choose where to sit based on how safe or protected I feel, Threat in Faces: I study people's faces and body language to detect if they are a threat

Vignette:
Ahmed is a 19-year-old Middle Eastern man who grew up in a household where physical abuse by his caregiver was an all-too-familiar occurrence. The violence was unpredictable and often followed arguments between family members, leaving Ahmed feeling perpetually on edge. His traumatic experiences have left him with persistent symptoms that have significantly impacted his daily life. Ahmed's triggers are rooted in the memories of those abusive episodes. When he hears or witnesses arguments, a flood of anxiety surges through him as he relives the fear and helplessness he felt during childhood. Even hearing someone cry can send him into a panic, as it reminds him of the tears he shed when his caregiver was abusive. The unexpected touch from anyone—a pat on the back or an unintended brush—can provoke intense discomfort because such touches often preceded physical violence in his youth. Now working as an environmental scientist, Ahmed navigates daily life with great caution. He avoids any situation that might involve disagreement or confrontation at work, which has led to him missing out on valuable collaborative opportunities and career advancement. His fear of conflict is so ingrained that he has developed a habit of always sitting in the corner during meetings where his back is pressed against the wall. This physical positioning gives him a sense of security, as it allows him to monitor everyone around him. Ahmed also tries to avoid being alone whenever possible. He finds solace in having someone nearby, even if just for company and perceived protection. His fear of isolation makes it difficult for him to focus on his work or relax during breaks when he is by himself. This avoidance has strained his relationship with his wife; she often feels neglected as Ahmed’s constant need for her presence can be overwhelming. The cumulative impact of these behaviors has left Ahmed feeling isolated and anxious, even in environments that should feel safe. His intense monitoring of people's faces and body language during interactions at work further reinforces his belief that others may pose a threat. He studies every facial expression and gesture, always on the lookout for any sign of hostility or displeasure. Ahmed’s avoidance strategies have taken a toll on his personal life as well. His wife has noticed his tendency to avoid social gatherings and group activities, which has led to misunderstandings and tension in their relationship. She feels that he pulls away from her emotionally, making it difficult for them to connect and share experiences together. Despite his best efforts to manage his symptoms, Ahmed's anxiety continues to grow. The stress of constantly monitoring his environment and avoiding potential triggers is taking a significant toll on his mental health and daily functioning. What frightens him most is the fear that he will never be able to trust others or feel safe again, leading him to seek professional help. Ahmed hopes for a way to manage his symptoms so that he can lead a more fulfilling life without constantly feeling on edge. He wants to reconnect with his wife and find ways to navigate daily life without avoiding every potential source of conflict or threat. The prospect of therapy offers him the opportunity to address these fears and regain control over his life, giving him hope for a future where he feels secure and connected.
